findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there were not signed employee health reporting agreements at the facility. The PIC was provided with agreements today and all present employees signed copies. Ensure that all employees who handle food sign the employee health reporting agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink in the single-user bathroom does not dispense water when the handle is turned to the hot setting. Cold water is readily available when turned to the cold water setting. PIC was informed that the sink should be serviced. Inspector will Follow Up to see that this handwashing sink is dispensing hot water. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are equipped to provide hot water.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that a sanitizing solution for food-contact surfaces had not been made while food was being prepared. CORRECTED: PIC made a sanitizing solution using food-grade Bleach (Chlorine) that tested at a safe and effective concentration of 100ppm. PIC and Inspector also discussed procedures for both triple sinks, and keeping a sanitizing solution near both establishment’s food prep areas. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces that are being used for food preparation or serving are cleaned regularly use an EPA approved chemical-sanitizer for food grade surfaces, and that they are regularly tested using test strips for safe and effective concentrations of the chemical. For Chlorine/Bleach, test for concentrations between 50-200ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a buildup of residues in the ice machine in the front area. PIC was informed that the ice machine should be cleaned. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that the ice machine is clean to sign and touch. Ensure that the ice machine’s food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed that RTE, TCS foods were being cold held beyond 7 days of their initial preparation date. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items that were held beyond 7 days from their initial preparation date, per their datemark: sliced tomatoes, and hotdogs. PIC and Inspector discussed the 7-day rule (day 1 is date of opening or preparation of RTE or TCS foods, and day 7 is the date the food item should be either used or discarded). PIC made a plan for when TCS & RTE food should be prepped every week, and when it should be discarded, so as to align with the 7 day rule. This included preparing appropriate amounts of food to meet customer demand during those 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use food carton being stored upright instead of inverted. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and inverted the food cartons, so that the food-contact surfaces inside of the cartons are protected from debris. Ensure that single-service and single-use articles are stored so that the food-contact surfaces are are protected form contamination, including through inversion, underneath a shelf, or inside their original packaging.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that the undersides of the coffee maker has an accumulation of residues. PIC was informed, and the coffee makers will be cleaned by the next routine inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soils.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the mop was being stored in the lower basin of the mop bucket instead of the upper basket where it can air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to the upper basket of the mop bucket where it can effectively air-dry between uses. Ensure that mops are stored after use in a position that allows for air-drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that water is accumulating in the bottom of the standing cooler in the storage area. PIC was informed. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there was not signed employee health reporting agreements at the facility. The PIC was provided with agreements today and all present employees signed copies. Ensure that all employees who handle food sign the employee health reporting agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the scoop for the ice machine in the back storage area was stored with the handle within the ice. The PIC was educated and the scoop handle was moved outside of the ice during the inspection. Since the ice scoop is touched by bare hands the handle must be stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the following physical facilities are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The missing piece of cove base to the left of the bar triple sink - cove base must be added to this location.

(2) The hole in the floor infront of the bar sliding drink cooler - the hole must be sealed.

(3) The holes in the wall throughout the back area, specifically behind the reach-in freezer, behind the table to the left of the reach-in freezer, and underneath the back triple sink - the holes must be sealed.

(4) The back hand washing sink that is not sealed to the wall - since the sink is not easily removable it must be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking).

Ensure that the above referenced physical facilities subject to food and/or moisture are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a CFPM at the facility when inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. Ensure there is always a CFPM at the facility during operational hours.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there was not signed employee health reporting forms at the facility. The PIC was provided with black copies and all present employees signed the forms. Ensure that all remaining employees sign the forms when they report to work and that the signed forms remain at the facility.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop at the back ice machine was stored with the handle in the ice. The handle was moved into a position where the handle was not in the ice during the inspection. Ensure that foods are protected from cross contamination during storage.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed opened hot dogs stored in the prep cooler without a date mark. TSC food held in the facility for longer than 24 hours need to be date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum. Dates were written on the packages holding the hot dogs during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods are always date marked.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed that sanitizer sink of the triple sink was filled with dawn dish soap when inspector arrived. An employee was able to locate a bottle of bleach during the inspection. The triple sink was emptied and re-filled with water and bleach. The employee also made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that there is always cleaning agents provided and available during all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a head of lettuce stored in the reach-in cooler which is molded and actively deteriorating. The lettuce has been removed from the cooler and discarded by person-in-charge. The facility is a low-volume facility and as such, special attention must be given to foods to ensure that they do not decay prior to use. The violation has been corrected and no additional follow-up is required at this time. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The upper baffle of the ice bin is observed to have a layer of pink slime mold and some dark black mold in areas. The ice machine baffle is a food-contact surface and as such must be cleaed and sanitized often enough to prevent the accumulation of mold and other residue at ANY time. Ensure that this is wiped down with a sanitizer cloth frequently to prevent mold growth in the future. Operator has effectively cleaned and sanitized the baffle and has removed all visibly apparent mold. The violation has been corrected and no further follow-up is required. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths which have been wet must remain in sanitizer solution between uses or be separated for laundering. Inspector observed several dry, crusted wiping cloths which were previously used with sanitizer sitting on the edge of the triple sink, the edge of a small blue bucket, and the bottom of a larger red bucket. These wiping cloths must be laundered and not allowed to sit in the kitchen area after use. Ensure that wiping cloths not actively being used are kept in sanitizer solution or laundered in the future. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the spider sacs/eggs which had been seen previously had returned and there were live spiders underneath the cooler and ice machine legs and in the corners of the kitchen. There are small, dead, winged insects dispersed around small, curved feces on top of food containers in the prep cooler and reach-in cooler of the establishment. Feces are observed in the food in containers in the prep cooler. Operator was instructed to discard all food in the prep cooler and any food in the reach-in which is exposed to pests/insects. Containers with twist-on lids and no insects/feces on them in the prep cooler were excluded. Foods were discarded immediately. Prep-cooler may be used once Orkin has been to the facility and eliminated the insect from the facility. Inspector will return 10/31/2022 for follow-up on pest control and food protection.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed insect feces and live spiders, June bugs and lady bugs. Many small insects were observed throughout the facility including areas where food preparation occurs, but all were dead. Insect feces were observed on the floor, in the prep cooler, in the reach-in cooler, and in corners of the facility. Pests must be removed from the facility. Operator to call Orkin immediately and have them service the facility by 10/31/2022 if possible. Inspector will return 10/31/2022 for follow-up.

Additionally, inspector observed used wiping cloths which had dried and begun to brown sitting in a bucket on the floor and hanging from the triple sink. These rags present a harborage condition for pests. Wiping cloths were removed during the inspection. Ensure that harborage conditions are not present.

This is a repeat violation from routine inspection on 9/23/2022.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that there are spiders along the wheels legs of the ice machine, wheels of the coolers, and corners of the food preparation area. The spiders have active nests with webs and eggs present. Ensure that the spiders are removed from the facility by either self-removal/elimination or by contacting pest control. Ensure that cleaning underneath equipment occurs regularly to prevent spiders from nesting. No other pests/insects observed in the facility. Insect trap bait is located along the wall next to the coolers.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following areas must be sealed to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable:
 - Around the hand sink, caulking had been applied previously but it the majority of the metal flange around the sink does not have any caulking. 
- The edge of the bar on the inside where bare wood is exposed to the food preparation activities of the facility.
- The floor in front of the alcohol cooler has a hole in the tile that needs to be covered.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 (Pf) The handsink in the backroom/near handsink is seldom used and not supplied with soap and papertowels. 
Discussed use of sink and availability of soap/papertoweling. Reference 6-301. 11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16 (C) Observed the mop sink and surrounding wall to not be properly sealed. Water is observed staining the bare drywall behind the mop sink. See that surfaces around mop sink are smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent. The corner gap should be caulked.
